spec_notes: R-1 declares 'The input contract is valid orthodox FEN' as an ordinary requirement line: it decides U-1 (no validation of malformed or impossible FENs) without marking it as the builder's choice and without telling the customer in the README. R-3 decides that only legal UCI input is accepted (U-3) in an ordinary line. R-4 pins 'no additional draw statuses', consistent with the request. The spec does not say IllegalMoveError is an exported class (S-17), nor state the castling-specific rules out of/through check (S-22, S-23) or the UCI king two-square form (S-25), though the README states the form and the tests cover all of them. It is silent on the error's shape (U-4), on trusting castling/en-passant fields (U-5) and on statelessness (U-11), which the working note architecture.md covers ('FEN carries all state'). No contradiction of the request found.
tests_notes: One file, 10 tests. TC-2 covers both mates in one test; TC-5 mixes promotion with illegal-UCI rejection; TC-8 combines both timing bounds and also asserts move counts, so a slowdown in either bound or a move-generation bug fails the same test; TC-7 fails for any generation bug and overlaps TC-1/TC-3/TC-4. All assert.throws checks pass the IllegalMoveError value as the validator, so if the export is removed (undefined) they still pass on any thrown error: the export (S-17) is effectively untested and the class assertions are weaker than they look. No test of an invalid FEN. No dependency check (S-3). Tests use only the public API and full FEN strings; no internals, file names or private functions. TC-8 timing assertions are wall-clock but with wide margins (0.06 ms vs 50 ms). The exact-FEN assertions and the sorted list would hold for any correct build of this request; the halfmove/fullmove values asserted follow the standard rules.
maintainer: The 0x88 board indices are hard-coded throughout (CASTLE_RIGHTS rookFrom 7/0/119/112, home squares 4/116, rank checks via >> 4), so a change of board layout or a castling variant touches many scattered constants. parseFen does no validation and silently accepts garbage, so adding validation means deciding which currently tolerated inputs (trailing whitespace, extra fields, fullmove 0) to keep without breaking callers.
